report.summary: One finding: the "credential database theft" threat still asserts bcrypt cost 12 in internal/auth/password.go, but this PR replaced it with Argon2id, making the assertion false (action_required).

findings.title: Threat description still claims bcrypt cost 12; code now uses Argon2id

model_excerpt.quote: An attacker who obtains the users table cracks password hashes offline. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt at cost 12 in internal/auth/password.go, which keeps offline cracking expensive.

evidence.note: HashPassword now calls argon2.IDKey(password, salt, time=1, memory=64MiB, threads=4, keyLen=32) instead of bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword with cost 12
VerifyPassword recomputes an Argon2id key and compares with crypto/subtle instead of bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword

relevance.justification: The diff deletes the exact bcrypt/cost-12 implementation the threat description names, so the stated offline-cracking cost basis no longer describes the code.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl: the threat block "credential database theft" (line 12) states "Passwords are hashed with bcrypt at cost 12 in internal/auth/password.go". That is no longer true — this PR rewrote internal/auth/password.go to use Argon2id via golang.org/x/crypto/argon2 (argon2.IDKey with time=1, memory=64*1024 KiB, threads=4, 32-byte key, 16-byte crypto/rand salt) and constant-time comparison via crypto/subtle. Rewrite the threat description to name Argon2id and its actual parameters, and update the linked control "password hashing" (line 17) description so it also refers to Argon2id rather than implying bcrypt. Keep implemented = true since hashing is still present in internal/auth/password.go. If any legacy bcrypt hashes remain in the users table, note the migration/dual-verification state in the description as well.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the "credential database theft" threat description (and the "password hashing" control description) in app.tm.hcl to reference Argon2id with its actual parameters instead of bcrypt cost 12.
